api_stats.note: Full API surface is far larger than what's listed below (SSO/SAML, audit events, teams, translations, AI/Ask assistant, integration publishing, MCP server config, redirects, fonts, styleguides, adaptive-content, agent channels/findings/insights, git-sync imports). Those are enterprise/admin/AI surface with no clear Grasshopper parametric workflow and are excluded here; pr-spec Phase 3 will confirm final scope against stated workflows.

content_workflow_note: GitBook does NOT allow direct writes to a space's live content. GET /spaces/{spaceId}/content is read-only. All content mutation goes through a Change Request: POST .../change-requests creates one (like a git branch), POST .../change-requests/{id}/content applies a batch of content changes to it (like commits), optionally POST .../requested-reviewers and POST .../reviews for review, then POST .../change-requests/{id}/merge publishes it into the space's live content (like merging a PR). This is structurally identical to a GitHub PR flow and should drive the write-component model in Phase 3: Create Change Request -> Apply Content Changes -> (optional review) -> Merge Change Request.

resources.name: Content
resources.description: Read-only view of a space's currently PUBLISHED (merged) content — pages, files, reusable content blocks. Writes never touch this directly; see content_workflow_note.

resources.name: ChangeRequest
resources.description: The write path for all content. content body change endpoint takes a batch requests[]-style array discriminated by `operation`: update_page | insert_page | delete_page | revert_page | insert_files. Pages can be authored as Markdown (frontmatter for metadata) or a structured JSON document.

resources.name: Revision
resources.description: Read-only historical snapshots of a space's published content.

resources.name: DocsSite
resources.description: Published documentation sites (the public-facing output built from one or more spaces).

resource_hierarchy: -> DocsSite (publishes one or more Spaces publicly)

auth_details.change_request_write_restriction: Verified per-endpoint in openapi.json: create_change_request, apply_change_request_content, and request_reviewers only accept a 'user' token (personal access token, or OAuth-as-user with space:write scope) -- the integration/integration-installation security schemes are NOT listed for these operations, unlike every read endpoint. merge_change_request additionally requires change-request:merge specifically (separate from space:write) when using OAuth. Practical implication: GitBookConnect's Token input must be a GitBook Personal Access Token for any Change Request write to succeed -- an integration token will be rejected outright regardless of scope, and a personal token still inherits the underlying user's actual space role (Admin/Editor/Reviewer/Viewer), so a Reviewer/Viewer-role user will still be blocked.
auth_details.live_verification: User ran a live 5-step smoke test (GET /user, GET /spaces/{id}, POST .../change-requests, POST .../change-requests/{id}/content, GET .../change-requests/{id}) against the real API with a Personal Access Token on 2026-08-27. All 5 steps succeeded -- confirms the change_request_write_restriction fix (personal token, not integration token) actually resolves the auth error, not just the schema analysis. Bonus finding: the ChangeRequest response object includes a urls.app field -- a direct link to view/edit the Change Request in the GitBook web app (e.g. https://app.gitbook.com/o/<org>/s/<space>/~/changes/<crId>/). Added as a URL output on Create Change Request and Get Change Request in plugin-spec.json.
